headline: HSC pass rate hits 22-year low with over 5 lakh students failing
summary: Bangladesh's Higher Secondary Certificate exams saw the lowest pass rate in two decades, with over five lakh students failing across nine general education boards. The number of students achieving GPA-5 also dropped significantly.
details: The pass rate in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations has fallen to a 22-year low, with more than five lakh students failing under the nine general education boards. The overall pass rate stood at 51.62 percent, a significant drop from 57.12 percent last year.

Historical data reveals that the last time the pass rate was lower than this year was in 2004, when it was 47.73 percent. This year, 5,07,281 out of 10,48,530 examinees failed in the general boards, marking the highest number of unsuccessful candidates in the BANBEIS data series since 1990.

Across all 11 education boards, including Madrasa and Technical boards, a total of 5,94,113 students failed, an increase from 5,08,701 last year. The combined pass rate for all boards was 52.12 percent, down from 58.83 percent in 2025.

The number of students achieving GPA-5, the highest grade, has also plummeted to an eight-year low. This year, only 40,084 students secured GPA-5 across all 11 boards, a stark contrast to the 69,097 who achieved it last year.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon acknowledged the unsatisfactory results and stated that the government plans to implement measures to address students' learning gaps and improve educational outcomes.

headline: 30+ RMG factories suspend operations amid wage protests
summary: Workers in Ashulia and Mirpur are demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000, leading to road blockades and clashes with police.
details: At least 30 garment factories in and around Kathgara, Ashulia, have declared a holiday today following protests by workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.
The unrest began in the morning, with workers from Naim Knitwear initially stopping work before expanding their protests to nearby factories.
Clashes broke out between workers and police, with reports of bricks and stones being thrown. One police officer is currently receiving hospital treatment after being struck on the head.
Industrial police also recovered three crude-bomb-like objects from the road in front of a Nasa Group factory in the Nishchintapur area of Ashulia around noon.
Simultaneously, RMG workers blocked several roads in Dhaka's Mirpur area, causing significant traffic jams on the Dhaka-Tangail highway.
Workers are also demanding an end to blacklisting and a halt to arbitrary dismissals, citing frustration over the delayed formation of a minimum wage board.
The Ministry of Labour announced that the process of forming the minimum wage board would begin this Sunday, though workers claim the message has not reached them.
Police are continuing efforts to persuade workers to clear the roads and restore order in the area.
caption:
30+ garment factories shut down as workers demand Tk 30,000 minimum wage.

At least 30 garment factories in and around Kathgara, Ashulia, have declared a holiday today following protests by workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.

The unrest began in the morning, with workers from Naim Knitwear initially stopping work before expanding their protests to nearby factories.

Clashes broke out between workers and police, with reports of bricks and stones being thrown. One police officer is currently receiving hospital treatment after being struck on the head.

Industrial police also recovered three crude-bomb-like objects from the road in front of a Nasa Group factory in the Nishchintapur area of Ashulia around noon.

Simultaneously, RMG workers blocked several roads in Dhaka's Mirpur area, causing significant traffic jams on the Dhaka-Tangail highway.

Workers are also demanding an end to blacklisting and a halt to arbitrary dismissals, citing frustration over the delayed formation of a minimum wage board.

The Ministry of Labour announced that the process of forming the minimum wage board would begin this Sunday, though workers claim the message has not reached them.

Police are continuing efforts to persuade workers to clear the roads and restore order in the area.
